articles.title: Ron Howard Says a Jim Carrey ‘Grinch’ Sequel Won’t Get Made Unless ‘It Has a Chance to Be Great’: We’re Moving ‘Cautiously’
articles.summary: Months after a “How the Grinch Stole Christmas” sequel was announced, director Ron Howard is setting the record straight on what it would take for the follow-up film to actually come to fruition.
body: Howard continued, noting that the duo feels so “proud of the original movie.” “We feel so fortunate, because it takes a little bit of luck for a movie to come together and become an evergreen the way that film has. And the following, the fact that it’s become a tradition in a lot of households is something that means a great deal to all of us involved, Jim and I in particular.”

But Howard isn’t ruling out a sequel in its eternity. “We’re gonna move cautiously but hopefully toward another movie because we both believe in the premise,” he said. “With a little luck, we’ll get to revisit that world.”

The original Christmas classic first premiered back in 2000 and was a box office hit, earning more than $350 million. Carrey, who starred as the Grinch and would reprise his role for the sequel, has long been outspoken about the toll the specific effects makeup needed to transform into the green creature took on him.

articles.title: Don Toliver Announces Sixth Album ‘Nitrous,’ Due Next Month
articles.summary: Fresh off receiving five Grammy nominations, Don Toliver has announced that his sixth album “Nitrous” will be released on December 4 via Cactus Jack/Donnway & Co/Atlantic Records. “Nitrous,” which Toliver has been teasing for some time, was recorded, produced and engineered entirely by himself.
body: To coincide with the album’s release, Toliver will make his “Saturday Night Live” debut on December 5. “Nitrous” features the new single “Party With the Boys,” which dropped this past Friday along with a Tyler Ross-directed video featuring Bam Margera.

Toliver is coming off of a red-hot year in the wake of his fifth album “Octane,” which was released this past January and bowed atop the Billboard 200. The project featured the hit single “E85” that reached No. 3 on Billboard’s Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart and No. 15 on the Hot 100. The Houston rapper spent much of the year on the road as part of his “Octane World Tour,” which had a first run of arena shows from May to July before picking back up for a “Nitrous: New World Tour” addendum to the trek from August through the end of November, when he’ll wrap the shows at London’s O2 Arena.

Yesterday, Toliver made waves with a substantial five nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards. In addition to best new artist, Toliver was nominated for best rap album with “Octane”; best rap performance with “Body”; and best rap song and best melodic rap performance with “E85.”

articles.title: Longtime Exec Howard Lee Departs as Skydance Confirms New Cable Structure and Division Name Under Channing Dungey
articles.summary: Skydance’s merged cable networks has a new division name: Skydance Global Cable Media. Warner Bros. TV Group and U.S. Networks head Channing Dungey also revealed the structure under the new entity, which combines the Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Global cable networks under one roof.
body: “One of the hardest parts of any transition is saying goodbye to talented leaders who have contributed so much and, just as importantly, have been trusted colleagues, friends, and mentors,” Dungey said in a memo to staff. “I want to express my sincere thanks to Howard Lee for his excellent leadership. I’m deeply grateful for the immense talent, commitment, and passion he brought to Warner Bros. Discovery’s US Networks over the years and wish him the best in his future endeavors.”
As part of merging a huge portfolio of more than 50 cable networks, Dungey divided them into four buckets: unscripted lifestyle, broad-based entertainment, talent/music/live and comedy/animation.
In unscripted lifestyle, Food Network prexy Betsy Sanner Ayala will add Discovery, HGTV and Magnolia oversight, with Discovery head of content Joe Boyle reporting to her.
In broad-based entertainment, TNT/TBS/ID president Jason Sarlanis will also now oversee TLC, with TLC head of content Alon Orstein reporting to him.

articles.title: Thom Velde, Former AMC Theatres Executive, Dies at 83
articles.summary: Thomas Velde, who served as head film buyer at AMC Theatres during his 27 years at the exhibitor, died Oct. 31. He was 83. Velde died of cancer at his home in Rancho Mirage, Calif..
body: Velde is survived by his wife, Deborah; his daughters, Andrea Ter-Velde and Courtney Ter-Velde, and their husbands, John McLoughlin and Greg Horton; his son, Sam; stepsons Matthew Castillo and Spencer Castillo and their wives, Crissy Castillo and Claire Castillo; grandchildren Aubrey Long and Jack Long; and step-grandchildren Jackson Castillo, Sammy Castillo, Cruz Castillo, Bianca Castillo and Capri Castillo.

A celebration of life will be held Dec. 8 at 3 p.m. at Woodland Hills Community Church. Donations can be made to the Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Foundation or the Motion Picture and Television Fund, both of which serve the industry community Velde was a part of.

“Thom was an avid golfer and a devoted college football fan,” his family noted. “Above all, he loved his family and friends, who will remember his strength of character, his generosity and the way he made time for the people in his life. He was always willing to lend a hand and had a special gift for keeping friendships alive over the years.”

articles.title: Call my (estate) agent! Why celebrities are always buying each other’s homes
articles.summary: If you’re seeking a discreet mansion with secluded grounds and plenty of room for your own memorabilia, you may want to remember Joe Pesci’s mistakes before trying the open market. Last year, Austin Butler bought a mansion from Brad Pitt.
body: If this makes it sound to you as if there are only a handful of celebrity-friendly homes on earth, and celebrities spend their lives swapping them around among themselves, then you’re right.

According to Mohamed Mussa, the managing director of Chestertons Global, this is partly by design. In an op-ed that has been doing the rounds, Mussa explains that celebrities often require things in properties that civilians like us might not consider, such as gated entrances, secluded grounds, space for staff and layouts designed to keep fans at bay.

“In 2020, Los Angeles City Council passed an ordinance allowing tour buses to be banned from residential streets judged unsafe,” he explains, which has to be useful. I once had a fairly major freakout after buying my house because I didn’t check the details properly and missed that the plumbing under my kitchen sink consisted of an Evian bottle sellotaped to a pipe. Imagine how much worse it would be to buy a house and realise that a packed bus parks outside your front door three times a day so that tourists can try and take a picture of you putting the washing out.
points: If you’re seeking a discreet mansion with secluded grounds and plenty of room for your own memorabilia, you may want to remember Joe Pesci’s mistakes before trying the open market.

articles.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping review – surreally awful prequel to the Katniss Everdeen era
articles.summary: Overwrought and boring, this nadir of a prequel to the Games’ death match saga is nothing but a cash grab for an exhausted franchise. Here is yet another iteration of the utterly exhausted, unbearably extended and now surreally boring Hunger Games franchise, based on the YA bestsellers by Suzanne…
body: Well, “reaping” in fact refers to an annual process by which ordinary smudgy faced, raggedy clothed people are chosen at random for compulsory participation in this futurist dystopia’s brutal, televised survival contest to the death: a bread-and-circuses nightmare with which the rulers keep the populace in a cowed and pacified state. In this Darwinian process, competitors strategically team up with (and then betray) some players against others in the short term, to stay in the game.

As ever, the “televisual” aspect of this is represented in the retro-style TV screens, but no one is ever shown actually watching these Games; Haymitch and his proletarian, quasi-hillbilly community don’t have TVs, but where is the middle class who are supposedly glued to their sets? Jesse Plemons is marginally less caricatured and tiresomely ridiculous as the organiser Plutarch Heavensbee, the younger version of the role earlier played by the late Philip Seymour Hoffman. But, really, this film has no actual interest and no authentic reason to exist, other than to gouge an income stream out of its fanbase.
points: Overwrought and boring, this nadir of a prequel to the Games’ death match saga is nothing but a cash grab for an exhausted franchise.

articles.title: 'Real life ghost story' inspires new TV drama in Welsh countryside
articles.summary: The "real-life ghost story" of a family who experienced "inexplicable" things is turned into TV drama.
body: The "real-life ghost story" of a family who experienced "frightening, inexplicable" things after moving to the countryside has been turned into a new TV drama.

The Witch Farm tells the "truly nightmarish" tale of Liz and Bill Rich who left London with their son Jonathan for a remote farmhouse in the foothills of the Brecon Beacons, determined to make a fresh start.
At first the isolation felt like freedom, but the family claimed things began to happen around the house leading them to feel increasingly scared.
Writer and creator, Danny Robins, met Liz who told him "her incredible story", becoming a four part series he beleives will "really surprise people".

articles.title: ‘Sorry, I’m still in love with Daniel Craig’: Ralph Fiennes, Brad Pitt and more react to Robert Pattinson as James Bond
articles.summary: Former 007 George Lazenby was supportive while The Lighthouse director Robert Eggers reveals what Pattinson was doing when the news broke • Robert Pattinson is James Bond. What happens next? • Peter Bradshaw’s take • Pattinson’s journey to James Bond • Behind Bond’s bankability.
body: Film industry figures including Ralph Fiennes, Brad Pitt and former Bond actor George Lazenby have reacted to the news that Robert Pattinson has been cast as the new 007.

Pitt was asked about Pattinson while promoting his new film, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, and responded: “I think it’s a great choice. I love what that guy’s been doing. He’s been making such interesting choices, and then for him to balance it out, it’s really cool.” Pitt then made a playful pitch for a villain role in Bond 26, winking at the camera and saying: “Get Denis Villeneuve on the flip phone. Let’s go.”

Fiennes, meanwhile, was being interviewed with his castmates from The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (in which he plays President Snow) on Sirius XM, and initially appeared somewhat downbeat, saying: “I’m sorry. I’m in love with Daniel Craig still. It’s hard. I’ve got the wrench in my heart.” But Fiennes, who played Gareth Mallory (who became secret service chief M) opposite Craig in Skyfall, Spectre and No Time to Die, added: “[Pattinson] is a great actor. I’m sure he’ll be great.”
points: Former 007 George Lazenby was supportive while The Lighthouse director Robert Eggers reveals what Pattinson was doing when the news broke • Robert Pattinson is James Bond.

articles.title: University pauses Shakespeare move after backlash
articles.summary: The planned move from Mason Croft is paused while the university explores future options.
body: The University of Birmingham has paused plans to move the Shakespeare Institute from Stratford-upon-Avon to Birmingham amid growing opposition to the proposal.

The university said it would spend the next six months working with partners including the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC) and the Shakespeare Birthplace Trust to explore the institute's future in Stratford.
The decision comes after criticism from Stratford-upon-Avon MP Manuela Perteghella and a petition that attracted more than 12,000 signatures.
The move from its home at Mason Croft had been due to take place in September.

articles.title: ‘Mick Jagger should fold up his penis and go home’: the caustic genius of music critic Robert Christgau
articles.summary: Beloved for his savage takedowns and rhapsodic raves, the legendary Village Voice reviewer opens up in a candid new documentary. Rows and rows of CDs, albums, cassettes and books creak and groan on shelves that snake around the walls and choke the halls of an apartment in New York City’s East…
body: Welcome to the lair of Robert Christgau, the self-declared “Dean of American Rock Critics”, as seen in a new documentary provocatively titled The Last Critic. “Bob is someone who has probably listened to more music, and published more words about music, than anyone to walk the face of the earth, and he’s still doing it in his mid-80s,” says Matty Wishnow, who directed the film. “It’s a career that’s both unprecedented and unrepeatable.”

Wishnow says he was inspired to make the documentary by the formative influence Christgau had on his taste growing up. “I would open his collections of Consumer Guides and wonder: ‘Why is Queen a C- and Billy Joel a B- while this group called the Roches is an A+?’ It scrambled my brain and made me think of the idea of commercial versus credible and popular versus sub-popular,” he says. “When people ask me why I’m not into Yes or James Taylor, I think 30% of my answer is personal and 70% is something Bob wrote that imprinted itself on me.”

articles.title: The Simpsons Season 46's Eric Bauza Tribute Explained
articles.summary: Shortly before his death, Eric Bauza guest-voiced two characters on The Simpsons, which paid tribute to the late voice actor at the end of the episode.
body: At the end of the November 15, 2026, episode of "The Simpsons," the show added a credit that read "In loving memory of Eric Bauza." This was a tribute to one of the finest voice actors of his generation, who died suddenly at the age of 46 from hypertensive cardiovascular disease. If his name is unfamiliar to you, his work most assuredly is not. Bauza voiced Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Marvin the Martian, Tweety, Elmer Fudd, Foghorn Leghorn, Porky Pig, Road Runner, and others for Looney Tunes. And it just so happened that he made his posthumous "The Simpsons" debut a few weeks after his death.

It's not hyperbole to say that Bauza possessed the vocal chameleon gifts of greats like Phil Hartman ( who wanted to play his "Simpsons" character Troy McClure in a live-action movie ), Harry Shearer, and Phil Hendrie. But what's most amazing to me is that he measured up to arguably the best ever to do it.
